claims.text: MoNbTaW is a bcc refractory high-entropy alloy.
A water-quenched MoNbTaW or similar bcc RHEA exhibits minimal chemical short-range order and high lattice disorder.
Controlled thermal aging can induce specific L12- or L11-type SRO motifs in a bcc RHEA without causing long-range phase separation.
Rapid quenching preserves the SRO state produced by aging.
Significant SRO suppresses lattice thermal conductivity relative to a chemically disordered RHEA state.
The effect of SRO on lattice thermal conductivity is non-monotonic and depends on SRO correlation length relative to phonon mean free path.
Short-correlation-length SRO behaves as a point-defect-like phonon scatterer because of local mass and strain-field fluctuations.
Point-defect-like scattering by short-range SRO suppresses lattice thermal conductivity.
Larger, more periodic SRO domains can produce phonon band folding or partial phononic band gaps.
SRO-induced band folding or band gaps can reduce transport density of states or alter phonon group velocities.
As SRO correlation length increases, reduced scattering efficiency can cause lattice thermal conductivity to plateau or recover after an initial decrease.
The predicted conductivity-versus-correlation-length curve contains a local minimum separating scattering-dominated and ordering-dominated regimes.
Thermal transport in the fully disordered baseline is governed primarily by alloy mass-variance scattering and point defects.
Measurements at 50 K isolate lattice thermal conductivity from electronic contributions in metallic RHEAs.
Measurements near 1000 K probe interactions between SRO and high-frequency phonons.
At low temperature, phonon-phonon Umklapp scattering in the target RHEAs is significant but not dominant.
The hypothesis does not apply when SRO development causes macroscopic phase separation.
EXAFS is sensitive to local chemical bonding preferences associated with SRO.
SANS, EXAFS, and APT can quantify SRO correlation length or cluster size in MoNbTaW over a range below 1 nm to above 5 nm.
A monotonic conductivity decrease over the full correlation-length range, together with absence of band folding or gap opening, would reject the proposed ordering-dominated regime.
